chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about one who performs four Hajj pilgrimages, what is his reward? He said: 'O Mansur! Whoever performs four Hajj pilgrimages will never be afflicted by the pressure of the grave. And when he dies, God will form the Hajj that he performed into a beautiful image, from the most beautiful of images, between his eyes. It will pray in the midst of his grave until God raises him from his grave, and the reward of that prayer will be for him. And know that the prayer of one of those prayers equals a thousand units of prayer of the humans.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing four Hajj pilgrimages according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the unique spiritual protection granted to one who performs four Hajj pilgrimages, specifically shielding them from the constriction of the grave (*dagh-t al-qabr*). The narration describes a metaphysical manifestation where the Hajj itself appears as a radiant image that prays on the pilgrim's behalf until resurrection, with each unit of this divine prayer equating to a thousand units of human prayer, underscoring the immense reward of consistent devotion in Shia tradition.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-37 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil Khat’tab, on the authority of Safvan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Mansoor ibn Hazim, “I asked Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) what the reward of one who has gone on the Hajj pilgrimage for four times will be. The Imam (MGB) said, ‘O Mansoor! Anyone who has gone on Hajj pilgrimage for four times will never bear the pressures of the grave. Once he dies, his visits to the Ka’ba will appear to him to be the most beautiful people in his grave and will pray in the corner of his grave until the Resurrection Day, while he will be rewarded for these prayers. You should know that the reward of each unit of these prayers would equal the reward of one-thousand units of prayers said by men.’”
